title: Rapid Isolation of Lysosomes from iPSC-Derived Neurons for Proteomics
author: Ali Ghoochani
materials: Pre-chill all buffers, tubes, magnet, and centrifuge to 4 °C. ￼ Keep everything on ice and minimize time from harvest → beads. ￼ Label tubes for each sample (example structure used in the template: post-homogenization, whole-cell/whole-homogenate, beads, final IP). ￼

steps.title: Prepare and Wash Beads
steps.instruction: Prepare the anti-HA beads based on the intended downstream analysis.

substeps.instruction: Use 100 µL beads per sample.
Wash beads 3X: use PBS+PI for proteomics or cold MS-grade KPBS for metabolomics/lipidomics.
Resuspend beads to the original pooled volume.
Aliquot 100 µL of beads into a labeled 1.5 mL tube for each sample.

steps.title: Harvest Cells
steps.instruction: Collect cells from the culture dish while maintaining cold temperatures.

substeps.instruction: Place the plate on ice and aspirate media.
Wash 2× with ice-cold PBS (gentle).
Add ~950 µL ice-cold PBS+PI (proteomics) or KPBS (metabolomics) to the dish.
Scrape with a cell lifter and transfer the suspension to a pre-chilled 2 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 1,000×g for 2 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 950 µL ice-cold PBS+PI (or KPBS for metabolomics).
Remove 25 µL of the suspension to serve as the 'whole cell/homogenate input' control.

steps.title: Homogenize and Clarify Lysates
steps.instruction: Break open cells and remove nuclei and unbroken cells.

substeps.instruction: Homogenize the remaining suspension by passing it through an insulin syringe 2X, keeping it on ice and avoiding bubbles.
Centrifuge at 1,000×g for 2 min at 4 °C to clarify nuclei and unbroken cells.
Carefully transfer the supernatant (organelle-containing fraction) to the tube containing 100 µL washed anti-HA beads, avoiding the pellet.

steps.title: Capture Lysosomes
steps.instruction: Incubate the lysate with beads to capture lysosomes and isolate them.

substeps.instruction: Incubate on a gentle rotator at 4 °C: 10 min for proteomics or 3 to 5 min for metabolomics.
Place on a magnet and allow beads to collect (approx. 25 s).
Remove the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash Captured Beads
steps.instruction: Clean the captured lysosomes using the appropriate buffer.

substeps.instruction: Wash beads 3× with 1 mL cold PBS+PI (proteomics) or 1 mL cold KPBS (metabolomics/lipidomics).
During the first wash, remove any liquid trapped in the cap and pipet up/down consistently.
After the second wash, resuspend beads and transfer to a fresh tube for the third wash.
Remove all residual buffer after the final wash.

steps.title: Extract Analytes
steps.instruction: Perform one of the following extraction options based on the desired analysis.

substeps.instruction: Option A (Proteomics): Add 80 µL ice-cold 1× Extraction Buffer to beads, incubate 15 min at 4 °C, collect supernatant via magnet, and store at −80 °C. Process input control by adding 165 µL extraction buffer, spinning at top speed (~15,000 rpm) for 10 min at 4 °C, and storing supernatant at −80 °C.

Option B (Polar Metabolites): Resuspend beads in 50 µL freezing-cold 80% MeOH (with internal standards if used), magnet-separate, transfer MeOH extract to a new tube, and store at −80 °C. Extract whole-cell control with 80% MeOH, clear by top-speed spin (15,000 rpm, 10 min, 4 °C), and store supernatant.
Option C (Non-polar Metabolites): Follow the external protocol at https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5qpvor3dbv4o/v1.
